title: Reproducibility of Model-Derived Predictor Importance Rankings for Childhood Stunting Across Age Cohorts and National Survey Waves
description:
Analysis code for a measurement-validity study of model-derived predictor importance rankings for childhood stunting, using two harmonized waves of the Indonesia Nutritional Status Survey (SSGI 2022 and SSGI 2024). The code does not develop or validate a deployable prediction model: a gradient-boosted tree is used solely as a measuring instrument, and the object of measurement is the predictor importance ranking itself. Reproducibility is summarized by a single named estimand, the rank-based reproducibility coefficient, defined as the Spearman rank correlation between two importance profiles on the exact set of items shared by the two cells compared. The coefficients are descriptive statistics on a fixed, finite item set, so no interval estimate for a population parameter is reported; inference rests on randomization tests, and sensitivity to the composition of the retained item set is reported separately.

The pipeline partitions the analyzed records into four period-by-age-cohort cells (baduta 0-23 months and balita_tua 24-59 months, crossed with the two waves) and, under an anti-leakage protocol that excludes outcome-forming anthropometry, measures three layers of importance structure: redundancy among predictors, additive main effects, and pairwise interactions. It then quantifies within-cohort reproducibility across waves, replication of between-cohort differences, and sensitivity of the recovered structure to imputation. Two complementary robustness analyses provide the reference against which the observed cross-wave instability is judged: a subsample-seed noise floor over five random subsamples, which varies nuisance only, and a model-specification sensitivity analysis over seven specification arms differing in tree depth, learning rate and number of boosting rounds, class weighting, and random seed, which varies the model deliberately. Every seed, hyperparameter, and specification arm is documented, together with an explicit mapping from each script and output file to the table or figure it produces.

The harmonized master dataset holds 721,385 records from three national sources (SSGI 2022, SSGI 2024, and SKI 2023). This study analyzes the two SSGI waves only: 86,364 records from the Indonesian Health Survey (SKI) 2023 lie outside the two-wave design and are never loaded, and of the remaining 635,021 SSGI records, 1,283 have no observed stunting outcome, leaving 633,738 analyzed records across the four cells.
